_note_field: MAINTAINER-ONLY. `note` records why a card is modelled the way it is -- provenance, schema reasoning, what was deliberately not modelled. Never render it in the UI. `caution` is the user-facing field.
_business_note: `business` marks a card issued on business underwriting rather than personal. Absent means personal -- only the field's presence is meaningful, so there is nothing to keep in sync on seventy-eight records. It filters the catalogue and nothing else reads it: the ranker does not care whose name is on the account.
_common_note: `common` is a POPULARITY RANK, 1 to 82, and it is EDITORIAL. There is no public card-level ranking of US cardholders -- Nilson publishes issuer volume, not how many people hold a Freedom Unlimited -- so this is judgement, not a sourced fact, and it is the only field here that is. It orders the setup picker so a new user meets mass-market cards first. 21 to 40 were added on 2026-09-27 as the next twenty after the first, 41 to 63 on 2026-09-28 -- store cards, then the remaining tiers of airline and hotel programs already present -- and 64 to 82 later that day, the cards of issuers Caddy did not yet cover, so each batch ranks below the one before by construction. Re-rank it freely; nothing computes from it.
_only_at_note: `only_at` marks a STORE CARD: the merchant domains where it works, and nowhere else. The ranker drops the card from consideration on any other domain rather than ranking it on its base rate, because recommending a card the till refuses is worse than not mentioning it. base_rate is then the store rate. Store cards with no rewards at all -- Home Depot's, for one -- are deliberately left out: a card that earns nothing can never be the best card to use.
_comment: All 82 records verified against issuer sources; 5 on 2026-08-29, 6 on 2026-09-09, 5 on 2026-09-10, 24 on 2026-09-27 -- the twenty added that day, plus Blue Cash Everyday, Amex Gold, BofA Customized Cash and U.S. Bank Cash+, re-read because their categories changed -- and 42 on 2026-09-28: the store cards and the remaining airline and hotel tiers, then nineteen cards from Synchrony's general-purpose line, Barclays, USAA, Navy Federal and Bilt. The Bilt cards' offer terms could not be read (the link downloads a file), so their category definitions are unconfirmed; see their notes. Each carries its source_url.
